title: Histochemical and biochemical analysis of collagen content in colonic samples
author: Baidoo, Sanger, et al.

steps.title: Collect and prepare colon tissue samples
steps.instruction: Obtain macroscopically normal colon tissue from surgery for non‑obstructed bowel cancer, at least 5–10 cm away from the tumour, after written informed consent; verify patient records for medication, comorbidity, and absence of prior chemoradiotherapy or active inflammatory colonic disease; cut each sample to approximately 10 × 10 mm, fix, process, embed transversally, and serially section.

steps.title: Perform Haematoxylin‑Eosin staining
steps.instruction: Manually stain sections in Harris haematoxylin, differentiate in 0.5 % acid‑alcohol, counterstain with eosin; dehydrate through a graded series of alcohols, clear in xylene, mount with Pertex (Sakura) and coverslip with a Sakura glass slide; nuclei appear dark blue and cytoplasm red‑pink/orange.

steps.title: Install ImageJ software and plugins
steps.instruction: Download and install the Java‑based ImageJ program developed at the NIH, version 1.53g, together with any required plugins for colour‑threshold analysis.

steps.title: Set spatial calibration in ImageJ
steps.instruction: Open the calibrated colour image, set the scale using a known distance (e.g., the 60 µm scale bar) so that all measurements are expressed in micrometres.

steps.title: Apply colour threshold to isolate collagen
steps.instruction: Choose Image → Adjust → Colour Threshold; set Threshold Colour to “Red”, Colour space to HSB; manually set Hue = 135‑195, Saturation = 25‑255, Brightness = 20‑255; click “Select” to generate a threshold image where collagen (blue) appears in red.

steps.title: Binarize the threshold image
steps.instruction: Convert the threshold image to an 8‑bit greyscale via Process → Binary → Make Binary, producing a binary image that represents collagen fibres.

steps.title: Select ROIs and measure collagen
steps.instruction: For each anatomical layer (mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa, taenia coli, circular muscle): use the Freehand (or Tracing) tool to draw the region of interest; open Analyze → Tools → ROI Manager, add the ROI, then choose Measure; after measurement, erase the ROI with Edit → Fill to prevent double‑counting before proceeding to the next layer.

substeps.instruction: Mucosa – draw area containing epithelium, lamina propria and muscularis mucosae
Submucosa – draw area between muscularis mucosae and circular muscle layer
Muscularis externa – draw area comprising circular and longitudinal muscle with myenteric plexus
Taenia coli (TC) – trace edges of the taenia coli towards serosa and myenteric plexus
Circular muscle (CM) – trace edges of smooth muscle towards submucosa and myenteric plexus, excluding ganglion

steps.title: Calculate collagen proportion per layer
steps.instruction: For each ROI, compute the proportion of positive (collagen) pixels or gray values relative to the total pixel area of that ROI; the software provides the positive‑pixel count automatically, yielding the total collagen content for each layer.

steps.title: Validate hydroxyproline quantification (optional)
steps.instruction: Cut a few 10 µm FFPE sections; the protocol is sensitive enough to quantify hydroxyproline content, with treated (histoclear) samples giving a mean of 37.93 ± 8.1 and untreated (paraffin) samples a mean of 36.99 ± 8.1, showing no significant difference.
